text:
maria: heads-up — we've got a steady mem growth on qwen-mqa when serving long rope-scaling sessions (100k+ tokens). KV resident pages keep increasing over ~30m runs :eyes:

maria: noticed this after the kernel-selection change merged last Thurs (runtime@6f4b2c9). spike shows up on canaries and a couple prod machines. logs show repeated: "evict() reclaimed 0/32 pages"

jin: yikes. can you paste the pmap/top snippet and the exact request pattern?

maria: snippet: 
```
PID   USER      PR  NI    VIRT    RES    SHR S  %MEM  TIME+  COMMAND
4123  rtech     20   0  64.8g  21.3g  1.2g S  12.8  02:12:33 runtime-worker
```
rope input is: many incremental inserts w/ rope-scale=1.5 per chunk, typical chat-like stream with prefix reuse. repro script: `scripts/repro/qwen_longrope.sh --tokens 120000`

ashwin: can you confirm whether this repros on llama/mistral too or only qwen-mqa? might be model-specific kv layout differences (MQA vs GQA).

maria: quick check — Mistral and Llama don't show the same slope. Qwen-MQA linearly grows, others flat. so likely MQA-specific.

samir: two immediate suspects: 1) kernel-selection change that switched to fused/packed attention kernel which changed KV page alignment, 2) batching heuristics that keep long-lived batches pinned and prevent sweep. did we change kv_compact_interval or sweep thresholds in that PR?

jin: i ran a quick bisect on the canary image. probable culprit is the kernel selector fallback logic: commit 6f4b2c9 toggled `prefer_packed_kernels=true` for qwen variants. forcing legacy kernels stops the growth.

maria: how did you force legacy?

jin: env override for now: `REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=legacy` when starting runtime. after that, mem stabilised under same load for 40m.

ashwin: interesting — packed kernels may change KV page fingerprinting which impacts slab coalescing. MQA's per-layer KV size pattern plus rope scaling produces many small allocations that fragment slabs. packed kernel changes chunk alignment so sweep can't coalesce adjacent freed pages.

eva: can we get a perf trace? sampling may show hotspot in the eviction/insert hot path. try `perf record -F 99 -g -p <pid> -- sleep 30` and upload flamegraph.

maria: attached quick profile (uploaded to #eng-runtime-artifacts). top hotspots: `kv_insert_shard`, `evict_pages`, and a new symbol in packed-kernel path `packed_attn::kv_map_write`

samir: confirms theory. fix options: a) revert prefer_packed_kernels for qwen-mqa until we add compaction-aware allocation, b) tweak slab coalesce window (lower `kv_compact_threshold`), c) add micro-reclaim after each request for long-running sessions.

jin: i opened a canary rollback PR to disable packed kernels for qwen-mqa and triggered a canary deploy. PR: https://git.redwood/runtime/pulls/4321

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for runtime image runtime:canary-4321 on cluster=us-west-2-canary :rocket:

maria: quick note — we should also add a regression test in perf harness: longrope qwen-mqa run for 1h and assert resident mem slope < 5MB/min.

ashwin: agreed. i can add a kernel-selection unit that validates allocation alignment invariants so future kernel swaps fail fast in CI.

eva: i'll file a follow-up to instrument compact stats (pages_coalesced, sweep_runs, failed_reclaims) into telemetry (per-model tag). helps triage future regressions.

samir: for immediate mitigation, leave rollback canary running and schedule a kernel allocator change (coalesce window + opportunistic micro-sweep) for next patch. put an oncall ticket and mark high-priority.

maria: thanks all — repro script and the perf dump linked in the thread. i'll add the memory assertions to the perf harness and assign the allocator patch to @ashwin.

jin: great. logging issue: RH-9876 (kv: qwen-mqa memory drift on packed kernels). I'll add bisect notes and attach the offending commit.

maria: leaving canary for now, will report in 30m. :mag:
